description.value: A preliminary fMRI investigation of neural correlates of provocation-focused rumination in women with borderline personality disorder and healthy controls.

spans.text: The rewarding nature of provocation-focused rumination in women with borderline personality disorder: a preliminary fMRI investigation

value: In response to provocation, participants with BPD (vs. controls) were expected to demonstrate higher activation in brain regions associated with reactivity to social rejection (AI, dACC, VLPFC).

All participants were expected to demonstrate greater activation in regions previously associated with anger rumination (dACC, DMPFC) during subsequent provocation-focused thought compared to neutral-focused thought; however, this effect was expected to be greater for participants with BPD.
Participants with BPD (vs. controls) were predicted to experience greater activation in brain regions associated with reward and pleasure (NAcc) during provocation-focused thought.

description.value: A pilot study of women with BPD and age-matched healthy controls, with assessment and scanning sessions; participants completed two fMRI tasks.

spans.text: The present pilot study examined neural correlates of provocation-focused rumination, relative to other forms of thought, in BPD.

name.value: BPD > Control between-group contrast during critical feedback

definition.value: BPD > Control between-group contrast in response to the negative essay feedback.

value: The BPD > Control contrast revealed a cluster of increased activation in the VLPFC, extending into the orbitofrontal cortex, operculum, and anterior insula, in response to the negative essay feedback.
These findings are consistent with the theory that individuals with BPD are more reactive to criticism, possibly including greater efforts to regulate their emotional responses.

name.value: BPD > Control contrast during provocation-focused rumination versus neutral condition

definition.value: BPD > Control during provocation-focused rumination compared with the neutral condition.

value: The BPD > Control contrast revealed greater activation in midline DMPFC during provocation-focused rumination as compared to the neutral condition.

Greater relative activation in regions of the DMPFC in provocation-focused thought in individuals with BPD, compared to controls, perhaps reflects greater intensity of engagement with the provocation stimuli for the BPD group.

definition.value: Group by condition interaction in right NAcc activation for provocation-focused and neutral-focused conditions.

spans.text: though the hypothesized group by condition interaction across all three directed rumination task conditions was not significant for NAcc activation, exploratory contrasts between the provocation- and neutral-focused conditions only revealed that while controls demonstrated no differences in reward-activation (NAcc ROI activation) between the neutral-focused and provocation-focused conditions, the provocation-focused condition produced significantly more activation in the right NAcc than neutral-focused thought for the BPD group.

Activation of the DMPFC and right anterior insula across both rumination conditions, compared to the neutral-focused condition, correlated with self-reported state rumination and trait-level displaced aggression.

value: When all three DRT conditions were included in the models, neither a significant group by condition interaction effect on the bilateral NAcc was observed nor a main effect of condition alone was observed.
In the exploratory provocation-focused and neutral-focused contrast, a significant group by condition interaction was found for right NAcc activation.

name.value: Provocation-focus versus neutral-focus in the BPD group

definition.value: In the BPD group, provocation-focus compared with neutral focus increased NAcc activation.

value: For individuals with BPD, the provocation-focus condition, compared to neutral focus, led to increased activation in the NAcc.
The provocation-focused condition produced significantly more activation in the right NAcc than neutral-focused thought for the BPD group.

description.value: Participants were directed to ruminate about provocation-focused, self-focused, and neutral topics.

spans.text: participants are directed to ruminate about three topics in succession: the prior provocation (provocation-focus condition), themselves (self-focused condition), and a neutral topic (neutral-focus condition)
provocation-focus condition
During provocation-focused blocks, participants read rumination prompts with statements instructing them to engage in anger rumination

description.value: For 90 seconds, participants covertly engaged in anger rumination about the earlier provocation, considering how they had been treated and whether the treatment was unfair or unreasonable.

spans.text: self-focused condition
During self-focused blocks, participants read statements instructing individuals to think about themselves

description.value: For 90 seconds, participants covertly thought about themselves, including what kind of person they were and why they responded to others as they did.

spans.text: neutral-focus condition
During neutral-focused blocks, participants read prompts with statements instructing individuals to reflect on neutral statements unrelated to the study

description.value: For 90 seconds, participants covertly reflected on neutral topics unrelated to the study, such as the layout of the local post office or a bus driving down the street.

spans.text: The task was implemented in a block design.

instructions.value: Participants were directed to ruminate about the prior provocation, themselves, or a neutral topic. Each block presented six statements for 15 seconds each, instructing the participant what content to think about.
